name: Uttara Kannada
headline: Forest-belt poverty and thin staffing, with only old out-of-school counts for the Sirsi area.
summary: Uttara Kannada has few documented exits: a 2014 state survey found only 686 out-of-school children in Uttara Kannada (the fewest in the state) and 1,066 in the Sirsi educational district, and COVID-era fears kept some Sirsi parents from sending children to SSLC papers. A 2023 High Court report found every government school in the district had toilets. Claims about Siddi girls and guest teachers in the deep-research report could not be tied to their cited pages and were dropped.

reasons.detail: The state's 2014 survey found Uttara Kannada had the fewest out-of-school children in Karnataka, with the Sirsi educational district higher.
During the pandemic some Sirsi parents withheld children from SSLC maths and English papers over health fears.

Many small Kannada-medium government schools in Karwar and Joida taluks were shut over 17 years, reportedly as parents shifted priorities. Closures can lengthen travel to the next school, though the source does not link them to secondary dropout.

A report says 35 government schools in the district recorded no admissions in one academic year; the department keeps such schools closed temporarily for up to three years hoping children enrol again.

reasons.factor: Adivasi learners cut off by COVID
reasons.detail: A state-level report lists Uttara Kannada among districts where first-generation tribal learners were pushed out of school by closures, no phones, lost mid-day meals and child labour. No Uttara Kannada village examples are given.
